Simone, it is Lucia from Madrid. Thank you for the review, because it found exactly what you were worried about. It seems that two of the buildings in Campinas have an unpaid property tax debt from two thousand and twenty. It is not huge, but it is real, and local counsel needs about three weeks to calculate it and to get the documents. So I'm afraid the closing will slip to the middle of April. Javier is not happy. His frustration is understandable, because he promised March to the board. Now, the difficult part is Ryan in New York. He told us that the end of March was his limit. When you call him, please be candid, but do not be blunt. Do not start with the delay. Start with what we found and why it protects both sides. And do not sound defensive: the review was the right decision. Give him a way forward: a new date, and a special indemnity for the tax debt. Then listen, and take his concerns on board.

Simone, it is Ryan. Thank you for the call this morning, and thank you for being candid with me. I will be honest too: my first reaction was frustration. My client is a fund, and funds hate setbacks, especially when they hear about them late. But you called before the email, you explained the tax debt clearly, and you did not try to hide it. That makes a difference. I talked to my client, and we can live with the middle of April, on two conditions. First, the special indemnity must cover the full amount of the debt, plus interest. Second, I need the documents from local counsel by the fifteenth, so my tax team can check them. If we can agree on that, I think this is a constructive way forward. Call me back when you have spoken to Madrid.

First, you prepare the facts: what happened, how big the problem is, and how long it will take. Then, you call before you send any email, so the other side hears the news from you first. After that, you give the news candidly, with a softener, like I'm afraid or it seems that. Next, you empathize with their frustration, and you do not get defensive. Finally, you offer a way forward and agree on the next step in writing.
